metadata.note: Yes -- Rochester, NY had a subway. The Rochester Industrial and Rapid Transit Railway (commonly 'the Rochester Subway') opened December 1, 1927 and ran about 8 miles from Driving Park in the northwest, through downtown (partly underground/in a cutting, following the abandoned Erie Canal bed after the canal itself was relocated to the new Barge Canal south of the city), to a loop terminus at Rowlands in Brighton. It closed to passengers July 1, 1956; much of its route was later repurposed to carry Interstates 490 and 590. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap, which tags the historic route directly as 'Rochester Subway' (abandoned/disused, including the tunneled downtown section). The stretch from City Hall through the Court Street tunnel and Meigs-Goodman to Monroe (~2km) has no connected 'Rochester Subway' track tagging in OSM for this specific downtown/tunnel segment (this part of the route is now buried under I-490) and is a straight-line approximation between the real, correctly-ordered station locations -- flagged honestly rather than guessed at closer precision.

https://www.planetizen.com/features/131382-book-excerpt-rochester-new-yorks-forgotten-subway (ridership peaked at 5.1 million/year in the 1940s; route later repurposed to carry I-490 and I-590)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_Park_station, Edgerton_Park_station, City_Hall_station_(Rochester), Court_Street_station_(Rochester), Meigs%E2%80%93Goodman_station, Monroe_station_(New_York), Culver_station, Highland_station_(New_York), Rowlands (individual station articles, used for precise coordinates)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API, overpass.openstreetmap.fr mirror): railway=abandoned/disused tagged directly as 'Rochester Subway' and 'Rochester Subway (historic)', including tunnel=yes segments under downtown; routed via Dijkstra shortest path through a graph of these real track ways between each station's Wikipedia-sourced coordinates. One short stretch near the Court Street tunnel mouth did not connect in this tagging and is a straight-line fallback.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency/timetable for any era; the Dewey Avenue surface-line ramp connection at Emerson station and the freight-only post-1956 life of the line are not traced on this map.

segments.note: The Rochester Subway (formally the Rochester Industrial and Rapid Transit Railway) opened December 1, 1927, built largely in the abandoned bed of the old Erie Canal after the canal was rerouted onto the new Erie Barge Canal. Ran about 8 miles from Driving Park in the northwest through 24 stops -- including a tunneled stretch under downtown at Court Street -- to a loop terminus at Rowlands in Brighton, connecting there with the Rochester and Eastern Rapid Railway interurban. Ridership peaked at 5.1 million riders/year in the 1940s; passenger service ended at 1:35am on July 1, 1956 as ridership collapsed with the postwar rise of the automobile. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
